text:
The Blue Jackets were a few minutes from a loss when Zach Werenski found a seam. Dallas had led 1-0 since Mikko Rantanen's wrist shot early in the third period. Then, at 16:46, Werenski scored on a backhand that our numbers gave a 5% chance of going in. Columbus took the game in a shootout, with Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scoring on their attempts while Dallas scored on none. It was a measure of revenge, too: Dallas had beaten Columbus 3-1 five days earlier.

The rest of the night was close, and the shot totals say so. Each team put up 62 shot attempts. In expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count, Columbus led 2.96 to 2.64. Our deserved-to-win figure, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, put the Blue Jackets at 56% and Dallas at 44%. So the better chances did land on the winning side, just by a thin margin. Werenski, the eighth overall pick in 2015 out of Michigan, played 29:24 and took five shots, and Columbus created 1.91 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.59 allowed.

The goalies kept it that way. Cam Talbot, who was never drafted and worked his way up from the AHL, stopped 27 of 28 shots and was named the game's first star. Casey DeSmith made 29 saves on 30 shots, about two goals better than the chances he faced would suggest, and he stopped Mathieu Olivier's 45% look in the third period. Neither power play scored, with Dallas 0 for 1 and Columbus 0 for 2. Columbus leaves with the extra point in a game it trailed late, and the facts we have show Dallas leaving with one point after outplaying no one by much and still falling short.
